text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Vietnamese press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet has called for better efforts to encourage the adoption of orphaned children by Vietnamese families.
-- Vietnam Railway hopes to reduce travelling time for the train journey between Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City by two hours.
-- The government has approved a continued tax exemption for materials and cars imported for the setting up of foreign invested enterprises.
-- An average of 200 work accidents happen each year in Vietnam resulting in the loss of more than 240 lives.
-- Hungarian and Vietnamese government officials have discussed economic, scientific and technical cooperation during a two-day meeting in Hanoi.
-- Vietnam's Interior Minister Le Minh Huong has ended a five-day visit to Laos to discuss security cooperation.
-- Vietnam reported 5,005 HIV carriers and 701 AIDS cases by mid February.
-- Ho Chi Minh City plans to move about half a million people from the central area to newly-established districts on the city outskirts.
-- The Ministry of Planning and Investment has announced restrictions on imported consumer goods, including electrical and electronic products.
